options.text: He gives advice to the President on legal matters

options.label: b
options.text: Is not entitled of audience except the Supreme Court

options.label: c
options.text: Cannot participate in the proceedings in the House of Parliament

options.label: d
options.text: Is a whole time counsel for the govemment

expl: The Attorney-General of India is the highest law officer of the country and the chief legal adviser to the Government of India. Under Article 76(3), the Attorney-General has the right to be heard in all courts within the territory of India in the discharge of his duties. According to Article 88, every Minister and the Attorney-General has the right to speak in either House, in a joint sitting of the Houses, and in any Parliamentary Committee of which he may be named a member, and to otherwise take part in the proceedings; however, he is not entitled to vote by virtue of this Article. The Attorney-General is not considered a “full-time government servant.” Subject to permission, he may also practise privately as an advocate.

stem: Who advises the Government of India on legal matters?

options.label: b
options.text: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court

expl: Under Article 76 of the Indian Constitution, the President appoints the Attorney-General to advise the Government of India on legal matters. A person qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court can be appointed as the Attorney-General. He is the first law officer of the Government of India and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

stem: Which officer of the Government of India has the right to take part in the proceedings of Parliament of India even though he is not a member?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: As a non-member, the Attorney-General can take part in the proceedings of Parliament. In this context, he may speak and participate in the proceedings. If the question is about participation in the proceedings of either of the two Houses of Parliament, the answer is the Attorney-General, because the Vice-President’s participation is limited to the Rajya Sabha. Also, the word “officer” has been used in the question, whereas the Vice-President is the Deputy Head of the State and the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Probably for this reason, the Bihar Public Service Commission treated option (b) Attorney-General as the correct answer.

stem: In the Indian Order of Precedence, who amongst the following comes first?

options.label: d
options.text: The Chief Justice of High Court

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The Table of Precedence relates to the rank and order of various office-holders in the Central and State Governments. The current notification in this regard was issued on 26 July 1979. According to it, the Chairman of UPSC, the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) are placed at the same level (9A) in the order of precedence, whereas the Chief Justice of a High Court is placed at the 14th rank within his/ her jurisdiction and at the 17th rank outside it. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

stem:
Arrange the following words in a logical and meaningful order:
1. vice President 2. President
3. Speaker 4. Prime Minister
5. Member of Parliament

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: In the Indian political system, as per the constitutional order of precedence, the President holds the highest position. After that, the order is Vice-President, Prime Minister, Speaker (Lok Sabha) and then Members of Parliament.
